channel.title: Tell Me More — Developer notes
channel.description: The hard problems, the design choices, and what changed because a reader said so.

item.title: Reading an 1871 dictionary with three OCR engines
item.description: Two readers agreeing isn't the same as being right. How glm, Apple Vision and the Internet Archive voted on 2,409 Bible names.

item.title: What was Rebekah's earring worth?
item.description: A question from a Bible study became a weights-and-measures reference, with ounces first, grams second, and the Bible's own prices beside today's.

item.title: Why Speak said "twenty-four thousand twenty-two"
item.description: One colon, read as a thousands comma. A small fix that matters to someone who listens instead of reads.

item.title: Tabs, not dots
item.description: A carousel's dots are a few points wide. For a reader with Parkinson's they may as well not be there.
